title: Import tariff on domestic firm investment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
This research scenario employs a Difference-in-Differences (DID) design to estimate the effect of the 2018 steel/aluminum tariff on capital investment at U.S. domestic steel producers. The key assumption of the DID method is the parallel trends assumption, which states that the trends in capital investment for the treated (steel/metals sector) and control (non-metals sectors) groups would have been parallel in the absence of the tariff. The DID method controls for time-invariant differences between the treated and control groups and time-varying common trends across both groups.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(plm)
library(broom)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s06_data.csv")

# Run the DID regression
did_model <- plm(y ~ treated * post, data = data, index = c("unit_id", "period"), model = "random")

# Print the results
tidy_model <- tidy(did_model)
print(tidy_model)

# Robustness check: Clustered standard errors
did_model_clustered <- plm(y ~ treated * post, data = data, index = c("unit_id", "period"), model = "random")
coeftest(did_model_clustered, vcov = vcovHC)

# Robustness check: Fixed effects model
did_model_fe <- plm(y ~ treated * post, data = data, index = c("unit_id", "period"), model = "within")
print(summary(did_model_fe))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient on the interaction term `treated * post` to be positive, indicating an increase in capital investment at U.S. domestic steel producers (treated) compared to non-metals manufacturers (control) after the 2018 steel/aluminum tariff. The magnitude of the effect is uncertain and depends on the specifics of the industry and the firms involved. However, given the protectionist nature of the tariff, it is reasonable to expect that domestic steel producers may increase investment in response to the increased demand or reduced competition. The estimated coefficient should be interpreted as the percentage point change in log capital expenditure for the treated group compared to the control group after the tariff.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=protected sector firms, control=unaffected manufacturers
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Tariff-protected firms increase capex relative to non-protected peers
_ground_truth.main_effect: 22% higher investment in treated firms post-tariff
